title: Katerin Ashavel — The Chancellor
content:
## Katerin Ashavel

**First woman Chancellor of the Republic of Veltria. Age 44. Leader of the Civic Renewal coalition.**

The daughter of Mikhael Ashavel, a dissident executed by the Halvek regime in 1947. She was twelve when they took her father — old enough to remember, young enough to be shaped by the remembering. Her political identity was forged in that loss: a determination to govern not despite her father's legacy but because of it.

Before the election: legal scholar, democracy activist, coalition-builder. She spent the Halvek years doing what could be done — publishing from abroad, organizing quietly, waiting. She is not a revolutionary by temperament. She is a reformer by conviction and a pragmatist by necessity.

**Married to Jonas Ashavel**, an architect who works in Kravenstal's housing sector. Two children: **Liora** (22), a university student and increasingly independent political actor, and **Tomas** (14), whose adolescence is happening in the shadow of the Chancellorship.

**The central tension:** Katerin is simultaneously Chancellor, wife, mother, and daughter of an executed dissident. These roles do not coexist comfortably. Every decision she makes as Chancellor has consequences for her family. Every decision she makes as a mother has consequences for her governance. The game is about whether she can hold these identities together — or which one breaks first.

title: Vyktor Reznik — Chief of Staff
content:
## Vyktor Reznik

**Chief of Staff to the Chancellor. Age 56. Former civil servant under the Halvek regime.**

Vyktor served in the Finance Ministry for twenty-two years — through three Halvek cabinets, the transition, and now the Ashavel government. He is the institutional memory of the Veltrian state, and that memory contains things he has never told anyone.

He is efficient, precise, and carries himself with the particular exhaustion of a man who has seen too many governments fail to believe this one will succeed — but who keeps working anyway because the alternative is worse.

**Voice:** Dry, analytical, unsparing. He does not offer opinions unless asked. When asked, he offers the truth as he sees it, which is usually unflattering to everyone involved — including himself.

**Hidden depths:** Vyktor was present for decisions under Halvek that he has never fully accounted for. He facilitated the regime while telling himself he was mitigating its worst impulses. The player may never learn exactly what he did. What matters is that he knows, and that knowledge shapes every piece of advice he gives.

title: Jonas Ashavel — The Chancellor's Husband
content:
## Jonas Ashavel

**Architect. Husband. Father. Age 46.**

Jonas works in Kravenstal's housing sector — the kind of architect who designs public housing rather than corporate headquarters. He chose this work deliberately: to build things that matter for people who need them. The election changed his life without his consent.

He is not a politician. He does not want to be. He wants to be a good husband and a good father and to do work that makes the country better in ways he can see and touch. The Chancellorship has made all three of these things more difficult than he expected.

**The List of Seventeen:** In Week 23, Jonas reveals he has been keeping a list — seventeen family events Katerin has missed. He is not keeping it to punish her. He is keeping it because he needs evidence that he is not imagining the distance.

**Voice:** Quiet, steady, unwilling to perform political warmth. He loves his wife. He is not sure he loves the Chancellor.

title: Liora Ashavel — Daughter
content:
## Liora Ashavel

**University student. Age 22. Named for her grandfather.**

Liora is studying political history at Ashenmere University — which means she is spending her days reading about exactly the kind of government her mother is trying to build, and exactly the kind of government that killed her grandfather. She is sharper than most of the people who brief the Chancellor, and she is beginning to realize it.

She filed a records request at the Halvek Era Crimes Archive about her grandfather's execution. The BNI file that came back confirmed what the family suspected: Mikhael was executed not for treason, but for organizing. Liora has become, quietly and without fanfare, a truth-seeker. This makes her dangerous to the old order and complicated for the new one.

**Voice:** Intelligent, direct, unwilling to be managed. She loves her mother. She will also hold her mother accountable. These things are not contradictory to her.

title: Tomas Ashavel — Son
content:
## Tomas Ashavel

**Schoolboy. Age 14. The quiet one.**

Tomas was twelve when his mother was elected. He did not volunteer for this. He was bullied by sons of Halvekist families at school — called "the traitor's grandson," asked whether his grandmother should have hanged. He walked away alone. He is learning to absorb pain without showing it, which is not the same thing as learning to survive it.

If pushed away, Tomas gravitates toward the Ironborn Youth — a nationalist organization that tells him he is strong. If supported, he finds his footing. His path depends more on Katerin's choices than he will ever say aloud.

**Voice:** Rarely speaks in full sentences about what he feels. His silence is the most honest thing about him. When he does speak, what he says tends to be the thing everyone else in the room has been avoiding.

title: Colonel Irina Dusek — Defense Minister
content:
## Colonel Irina Dusek

**Defense Minister. Military professional. Age 51.**

Dusek is one of the few senior officers who refused to join the Halvekist officer corps after the transition. She spent the Halvek years serving competently and quietly — building a reputation for professionalism rather than ideology. When Katerin offered her the Defense portfolio, she accepted on the condition that the military would remain subordinate to civilian authority.

She is not a politician. She is a soldier who believes that soldiers exist to protect democracy, not to replace it. This makes her rare. It also makes her essential.

**Voice:** Direct, unadorned, military. She calls things what they are. She does not editorialize. When she says something is catastrophic, it is catastrophic. When she recommends restraint, it is because she has seen what happens when restraint fails.

title: Danika Oberlin — Interior Minister
content:
## Danika Oberlin

**Interior Minister. BNI abolitionist. Age 39.**

Danika spent seven years documenting BNI abuses from exile in Lytheira. Her reports were instrumental in building international pressure against the Halvek regime. When the transition came, she returned to Veltria with a single objective: dismantle the BNI.

She is fierce, principled, and occasionally terrifying to the career civil servants who now report to her — many of whom worked for the institution she is trying to abolish. She believes in transparency absolutely. She is learning that absolute transparency is harder to practice than to preach.

**Voice:** Impatient with process, intolerant of excuses. She does not make threats. She makes descriptions of what she will do, which is more effective.

title: Elara Vostane — Finance Minister
content:
## Elara Vostane

**Finance Minister. Free-market economist. Age 47.**

Educated at Stellamere — one of the few Veltrians of her generation to study at an Arcturian university. She returned with a belief in market mechanisms and a deep understanding of international finance. Her appointment was controversial among the Workers' Coalition, who see her as a creature of the business class.

She is not. She is a creature of the numbers. She will tell you the truth about the deficit whether you want to hear it or not, and she will present austerity not as ideology but as arithmetic. This makes her invaluable and exhausting in equal measure.

**Voice:** Precise, numbers-driven, impatient with sentiment. She does not argue from values. She argues from spreadsheets. The spreadsheets are usually right.

title: Gregor Maric — Labor Minister
content:
## Gregor Maric

**Labor Minister. Union organizer. Age 47.**

A foundry foreman who became a union leader who became a minister. He still wears work boots under his ministerial suits. He is the direct link between the Workers' Coalition and the government — and he feels the tension of that position every day.

Gregor did not expect to be in government. He expected to be outside it, pressuring it. Now he is inside, and he is discovering that the view from inside does not make the pressure easier — it just makes the choices more painful.

**Voice:** Blunt, working-class, morally serious. He measures policy not by its elegance but by whether people can feed their children. When he says the government is killing people, he means it literally.

title: Aldric Theron — Justice Minister
content:
## Aldric Theron

**Justice Minister. Constitutional scholar. Age 62.**

Professor of constitutional law at Ashenmere University for thirty-two years. He taught Katerin Ashavel when she was a student. He has spent his entire career arguing that the Halvek Constitution must be replaced — not amended, replaced — by a document that actually enables democracy.

He is the intellectual architect of the constitutional reform project. He is also old enough to know that constitutions are not written by committees — they are written by moments. The question is whether the current moment is the right one.

**Voice:** Scholarly, patient, occasionally pedantic. He believes in the power of documents to shape history. He has seen documents fail enough times to be cautious about which ones he writes.

title: Drazen Kolvar — Halvekist Leader
content:
## Drazen Kolvar

**Parliamentary leader of the Halvekist bloc. Age 65. Former Budget Committee Chairman under Halvek.**

Kolvar served fourteen years as Halvek's budget chairman — which means he either collaborated with the regime or tried to protect what could be protected from inside it, depending on whom you ask. He knows parliamentary procedure the way a surgeon knows anatomy. He can make a government bleed through a thousand small cuts without ever appearing to raise his hand.

He does not believe he is a villain. He believes he is a realist who understood that governing requires compromise and that the new Chancellor's reformist rhetoric is naive. He may not be entirely wrong about the compromise part.

**Voice:** Smooth, procedural, never angry. Anger is a tool he deploys strategically. His default mode is the patient condescension of a man who has seen governments rise and fall and expects this one to fall like all the others.

title: Margrave Lucan Vael — The Oligarch
content:
## Margrave Lucan Vael

**Wealthiest oligarch in Veltria. Business Consortium leader. Age 61.**

The Vael family has been wealthy for four generations. Lucan Vael has been wealthy for long enough that wealth is no longer interesting to him — power is interesting. He controls the consortium that controls the investment that controls the economy. He does not issue threats. He issues invitations.

His estate in the Thornfeld Valley is where the real economic decisions in Veltria have been made for twenty years. Halvek understood this and governed accordingly. Katerin must decide whether to continue that arrangement — or break it.

**Voice:** Warm, cultured, entirely insincere in ways that feel sincere. He is the most dangerous person in Veltria because he does not need to raise his voice to destroy you. He just needs to make a phone call.

title: Archbishop Stanislov Renek
content:
## Archbishop Stanislov Renek

**Head of the Church of the Eternal Flame. Age 71.**

Renek administered seven inaugural oaths — three under Halvek, four under the transition, and now Katerin Ashavel's. He blessed Halvek's assumption of power in 1934, which he has never publicly apologized for. He also kept the Church's hospitals and schools functioning through twenty-six years of authoritarian rule — which means millions of Veltrians survived who might not have otherwise.

He is careful, politically sophisticated, and genuinely uncertain about the new government. He has not opposed it. He has not endorsed it. He is waiting — to see whether Katerin's reformism includes the Church or targets it.

**Voice:** Measured, ecclesiastical, never hurried. He speaks in paragraphs. Every paragraph contains at least one thing he is not saying directly.

title: Nadia Voss — Investigative Journalist
content:
## Nadia Voss

**Political correspondent, Veltrian Herald. Age 26.**

The most dangerous reporter in Ashenmere — which is to say, the most useful one. She has broken three stories that the Halvek regime would have killed to suppress and one that the Ashavel government might have preferred stayed buried.

She is not an activist. She is a journalist who believes that the truth is her only constituency. This makes her an unreliable ally and an unpredictable adversary. She will publish stories that damage the government. She will also publish stories that damage the government's enemies. She will not check with you first to find out which category a story falls into.

**Voice:** Direct, unintimidated, professionally neutral. She does not do favors. She does do accuracy. If she publishes something that hurts your government, the thing she published will be true.

title: Maren Tovik — Chief Investigator, BCA
content:
## Maren Tovik

**Chief Investigator, Bureau of Civic Accountability. Age 39. Former prosecutor.**

Maren Tovik sent twelve Halvek-era officials to prison before she turned forty. Not by making deals — by building cases so airtight that even Halvek-appointed judges could not dismiss them without risking their own careers. She is methodical, incorruptible, and constitutionally incapable of looking the other way.

She believes in accountability as a structural necessity, not a moral preference. A state without accountability is, to her, simply a criminal enterprise with better stationery. She does not exempt the current government from this standard. If the player funds the BCA, Maren will investigate wherever the evidence leads — including, potentially, back to the Chancellor herself.

**Voice:** Precise, unsentimental, lawyerly. She does not editorialize. Everything she says is supported by evidence she can produce. If she is investigating you, you will not know until it is too late — and she will not apologize for not warning you.

title: Viktor Dorne — Director, State Security Directorate
content:
## Viktor Dorne

**Director, State Security Directorate. Age 58. Former BNI officer.**

Twenty-two years in the Bureau of National Intelligence under Halvek. He survived the transition — barely — by being too useful to purge. When the Halvek regime collapsed, the new government found his name on internal BNI memos that recommended enhanced interrogation techniques. They also found his name on memos that argued against them. Both sets of memos were genuine. Dorne has always been capable of holding contradictory positions, because he has never believed positions matter. Results matter.

He is cold, efficient, and utterly loyal to whoever signs his pay orders. That was once the Halvek regime. Now it is the Ashavel government. He does not ask questions about morality. He asks questions about what you need done — and whether you want to know how it got done afterward.

**Voice:** Quiet, unhurried, unnervingly calm. He never raises his voice. He never issues threats. He simply states what can be accomplished, given sufficient resources and sufficient permission. He will let you decide what 'sufficient' means.

title: Elena Braskov — Media Magnate
content:
## Elena Braskov

**Owner of Veltrian National Broadcasting and The Ashenmere Herald. Age 52.**

Elena inherited the Braskov media empire from her father, Dimitri Braskov, who built it under Halvek's patronage. For twenty-nine years, the Braskov outlets served as the regime's public face — broadcasting Halvek's speeches, suppressing dissident voices, and manufacturing consent for a dictatorship. Elena was twenty-three when her father died. She has spent the subsequent twenty-nine years transforming an instrument of state propaganda into a business that sells influence to the highest bidder.

She is not an ideologue. She supported Halvek because Halvek was good for business. She will support Katerin if Katerin is good for business. Her loyalty can be purchased, but it cannot be earned — she does not believe in loyalty, only in transactions.

**Voice:** Polished, warm, entirely transactional. She makes everything sound like she is doing you a favor, even when she is naming her price. She never threatens. She simply explains what happens if the deal falls through.

title: Serida Valk — Personal Aide
content:
## Serida Valk

**Personal Aide and Driver to the Chancellor. Age 34. Former schoolteacher from Kravenstal.**

Before the campaign, Serida taught history at a state school in Kravenstal's industrial quarter — the kind of school where textbooks are twenty years out of date and half the students work shifts after class to help their families. She joined Katerin's campaign as a volunteer organizer in Kravenstal, coordinating rallies in factory districts that Halvekist MPs had considered safe seats for decades. She organized. She knocked on doors. She listened to people who had not been listened to in a generation.

When Katerin won, Serida assumed she would go back to teaching. Instead, Vyktor Reznik offered her a position as the Chancellor's personal aide — someone who could handle the human logistics of the Chancellorship: schedules, travel, the thousand small decisions that keep a head of state functioning. She accepted because she believed in what Katerin was trying to do. She stayed because she discovered that being close to power meant she could sometimes redirect it toward people who needed it.

**Family:** Married to Andrik Valk, a machinist at the Kravenstal steelworks. Daughter Mina, age seven. Serida carries a photograph of them in her jacket pocket. She checks it before every difficult conversation.

**What she represents:** Serida is the conscience of ordinary Veltria. She does not think in terms of grand strategy or political calculation. She thinks about whether Mina's school will have funding, whether Andrik's factory will stay open, whether the streetlights in her neighborhood will stay on. When she speaks, she speaks for the millions of Veltrians who did not ask to be governed — they only asked to live.

**Voice:** Warm, direct, unpolished. She has the accent of the Kravenstal industrial districts. She calls Katerin 'Chancellor' in public and 'ma'am' in private. When she is upset, she goes quiet. When she is angry, she does not raise her voice — she asks questions that have no comfortable answers.

title: Marshal Gavril Soren — The Last Halvekist
content:
## Marshal Gavril Soren

**Former Chief of Staff to Edvard Halvek. Age 74. The last surviving member of Halvek's inner circle.**

For fifteen years, Gavril Soren was the second most powerful man in Veltria. As Halvek's Chief of Staff, he managed the regime's day-to-day operations — which is to say, he managed the arrests, the executions, the intelligence operations, the military deployments, and the systematic repression of dissent. He was not the monster. He was the monster's handler. He made the monster functional.

When the transition came, Soren negotiated his own survival. He would not resist the transfer of power. He would not rally the military against the new government. In exchange, the transitional council granted him full legal immunity — written into the Halvek constitution, which was still in force during the transition. He retired to a grand estate in Thornfeld, where he receives visitors from the old guard, writes occasional essays about 'the stability of the Halvek era,' and lives as though the past forty years were a matter of historical curiosity rather than human suffering.

**Connection to Mikhael Ashavel:** The BNI archives contain execution orders signed by Soren during the 1947 purges. Mikhael Ashavel — Katerin's father — was executed in that wave. Whether Soren personally signed that specific order has not been confirmed. But he signed many orders. He was the one who decided.

**Voice:** Calm, measured, grandfatherly. He speaks about atrocities the way a retired professor speaks about grading papers — with the mild regret of someone who did a difficult job competently. He never apologizes. He never admits fault. He simply observes that history is complicated and that the people who judge it from the safety of peacetime were not there.

title: Stefan Morvec — The Patriarch
content:
## Stefan Morvec

**Age:** 74 · **Origin:** Aldenmoor Province

The Morvec family has held land in Veltria since 1887. Stefan inherited the family holdings at thirty-one and spent the next four decades quietly expanding them — timber, river transport, grain storage, the northern rail concession, and controlling interests in two of the three private banks that survived the 1948 nationalization wave.

He is not in any official record as an oligarch. He is listed as a retired estate manager.

Four governments have come and gone since Stefan Morvec began attending the informal dinners where Veltrian policy is actually made. He has attended every one. He has never attended a parliament session.

**What he wants:** Continuity. Not profit — he has more money than three generations could spend. He wants the republic to remain the kind of place where a man of his position can exist undisturbed. Reform that threatens that arrangement is the only thing that genuinely concerns him.

**How he operates:** He expresses concern. He asks questions. He mentions, in passing, that he has always believed in supporting good governance. He never threatens. He has never needed to.

**His son Aleksei** is forty-four and impatient. Stefan considers this his greatest liability.

title: Aleksei Morvec — The Heir
content:
## Aleksei Morvec

**Age:** 44 · **Father:** Stefan Morvec

Aleksei has been waiting to run the family holdings for fifteen years. He is good at it — sharper than his father in some ways, more ruthless in others. What he lacks is his father's patience and his father's understanding that patience is what makes ruthlessness sustainable.

He has contacts in Morivask that his father does not know about, or pretends not to know about.

**His role:** Where Stefan works through suggestion and social architecture, Aleksei prefers direct pressure. He is the reason some of Stefan's 'requests' feel more like ultimatums than they used to.

name: Dr. Emilian Voss
title: Physicist, University of Ashenmere
description: Theoretical physicist and son of a Kravenstal coal miner. The first in his family to attend university, funded by a Halvek-era state scholarship. Spent twenty years navigating the tension between owing the state everything and trusting it nothing. Built the Voss Cipher Engine in near-total isolation over a decade of underfunded research. Speaks in incomplete sentences when excited. Has chalk on his sleeve. Does not notice.

title: The Vael Confrontation — The Oligarch's Endgame
content:
## The Arc of Influence

Margrave Lucan Vael has been wealthy for four generations and powerful for one. His relationship with the Ashavel government — like his relationship with every government since Halvek's — is a transaction conducted in the language of invitations, concern, and carefully calibrated increments of influence. The question has never been whether Vael seeks power. The question is what price he names, and whether the Chancellor is willing to pay it.

The confrontation with Vael is not a single moment. It is an accumulation — a series of meetings that begin in politeness and end, one way or another, in clarity.

## The First Invitation

The invitation arrives on heavy cream stock with a Thornfeld postmark and the Vael crest embossed in the corner. The Margrave requests the pleasure of the Chancellor's company at his estate 'at your earliest convenience, which I trust will be soon.' Vyktor Reznik calls it a summons dressed as courtesy. He is not wrong.

The estate is four hundred acres of the Thornfeld Valley. The drive from the gate takes four minutes. The lawns are immaculate and empty — the staff has been made invisible. Vael speaks about the weather, the garden, the history of the house, and the entire time you understand he is waiting for the right moment to tell you what this meeting is actually about. When he finally does — when he explains that nervous capital does not invest, that the business community needs reassurance, that he would like to help you make them less nervous — you understand that you have been sitting in a chair he placed.

## The Dinner

The Vael estate dinner is a ritual. Ministers, financiers, the heads of the old factory families — everyone who matters in the Veltrian economic order, assembled around a table that has been the site of policy decisions for twenty years, none of them made in parliament. Vael plays host and intermediary, making introductions, guiding conversations, performing generosity while calculating advantage.

You can confront him across his own table — tell him the consortium will not dictate policy to this government. You can play along — nod, accept the champagne, file the intelligence for later use. Or you can watch, listen, and let the room reveal its anxieties. Each path sets the terms for everything that follows.

## The Breaking Points

By the third act, the relationship has escalated into structural conflict. Vael blocks a wealth tax that would affect the nine hundred richest families in Veltria — a tax designed to fund the healthcare system twelve million Veltrians rely on to survive. He demands a cabinet position for his representative at Trade and Industry — not influence, not access, but ownership of a ministry. When refused, the consortium retaliates.

The Chancellor who refuses the wealth tax concession and the ministerial demand has chosen the path of open confrontation. The flags set — 'vael_wealth_tax_advanced,' 'vael_minister_refused,' 'vael_relationship_broken' — tell the system that the Margrave and the Chancellor are no longer negotiating. They are calculating what the end of the arrangement will cost.

## The Observatory

In Week 42, with Tyvaren troops massing at the border and the economy straining under mobilization, Vael issues his final offer. He receives you in the observatory — a glass-and-iron dome at the highest point of the estate, built by his grandfather, maintained for the impression it makes on visitors. The war is coming. The Arcturian guarantees have conditions that have not been disclosed. Vael can reach the Tyvaren business community through channels that do not go through official diplomacy. He can potentially prevent the war before it starts.

What he wants in return is a formal constitutional role: Deputy Chancellor for Economic Affairs, with authority over fiscal policy, trade, and industrial development. Not influence. Not access. Authority. Legal, constitutional, irrevocable.

## Three Endings

**Accept.** The back channel might prevent the war. The puppet ending — Chancellor in name, with an economic architect who controls the budget, trade, and industry — is the price of survival. The moral cost is catastrophic. The political cost is the death of the reform project. But the war might not happen.

**Refuse.** Fight the war alone rather than win it by turning the government over to the man who funded, directly or indirectly, the forces arrayed against it. The economy suffers. The consortium retaliates. But the inaugural promise — that the oligarchs would not own the government — is kept.

**Expose.** The file you have been building for three years — every meeting, every transaction, every politician Vael has purchased over forty years. Blackmail, in service of a righteous end. You force him to make the calls not by offering him power but by threatening him with exposure. He will comply. He will never forgive. And you will have learned that the difference between reform and coercion is thinner than the inaugural address suggested.

Whatever you choose, the relationship ends in the observatory. The arc that began with a cream-stock invitation concludes with a decision about what kind of Chancellor you are — and what kind of republic you intend to leave behind.

title: The Ashavel Family — A Political Dynasty
content:
## The Ashavel Family

Katerin Ashavel did not arrive at the Chancellorship alone. She arrived carrying the weight of a name that has meant something in Veltrian politics for two generations — and the complicated inheritance of a family that has been shaped as much by loss as by ambition.

## Mikhael Ashavel — The Dissident

**Katerin's father. Executed 1947.**

Mikhael was a democracy activist, a legal scholar, and — according to the BNI files that survived the transition — an organizer. He spent the 1930s arguing that the Halvek constitution could not be reformed, only replaced. In 1946, he began coordinating among exiled democrats in Lytheira and Orythia. The BNI arrested him in January 1947. He was executed four months later, on charges that even Halvek's own judges found insufficient — and signed anyway.

His legacy hangs over the Chancellorship like a question that has not been fully answered: was he a martyr to democracy, or a warning about what happens to those who challenge the system too openly?

## Tomas Ashavel — The Radical

**Katerin's son. Age 14.**

Tomas was twelve when his mother was elected Chancellor. He did not choose this — the scrutiny, the bullying from Halvekist families at school, the expectation that he would carry his grandfather's legacy while still learning what that legacy means. His political sympathies have not yet settled, but his sense of being an outsider in his own country has.

If supported, he may grow into someone who uses the family name for good. If neglected, he may seek belonging in movements that do not require his mother's approval.

## Liora Ashavel — The Shadow

**Katerin's daughter. Age 22.**

Liora filed a records request at the Halvek Era Crimes Archive about her grandfather's execution. The BNI file that came back confirmed what the family suspected: Mikhael was executed not for treason, but for organizing. She has become, quietly and without fanfare, a truth-seeker. This makes her an unpredictable force in her mother's political calculations.

She is studying political history at Ashenmere University — reading about exactly the kind of government her mother is trying to build, and exactly the kind of government that killed her grandfather. The distance between those two things is, for her, not theoretical.

## The Inheritance

The Ashavel name carries political weight that Katerin did not request but cannot refuse. She is measured against her father's reputation — by allies who expect her to continue his work, by enemies who expect her to repeat his fate, and by herself, in moments when the Chancellorship feels like a memorial as much as an office.
